<svg xmlns=3D"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width=3D"20" height=3D"20" viewBo=
x=3D"0 0 24 24" fill=3D"none" stroke=3D"currentColor" stroke-width=3D"2" st=
roke-linecap=3D"round" stroke-linejoin=3D"round" class=3D"lucide lucide-max=
imize2 lucide-maximize-2"><polyline points=3D"15 3 21 3 21 9"></polyline><p=
olyline points=3D"9 21 3 21 3 15"></polyline><line x1=3D"21" x2=3D"14" y1=
=3D"3" y2=3D"10"></line><line x1=3D"3" x2=3D"10" y1=3D"21" y2=3D"14"></line=
></svg></button></div></div></div></a></figure></div><p><span>There=E2=80=
=99s a very cool </span><a href=3D"https://www.exploratorium.edu/exhibits/m=
achine-with-concrete">exhibit </a><span>in the San Francisco Exploratorium,=
 called =E2=80=9CMachine with Concrete=E2=80=9D. It=E2=80=99s a long series=
 of reduction gears with a running motor at one end, and a block of concret=
e at the other. One end is turning furiously, and the reduction in gearing =
means that the end will only turn once every trillion years or so (the web =
page says billion but the exhibit says trillion). It=E2=80=99s a fascinatin=
g display of entropy and thermodynamics, but I=E2=80=99ve also always seen =
it as a good illustration of the idea that activity (or motion) isn=E2=80=
=99t the same as progress.</span></p><p>I=E2=80=99m a very creative person.=
 OK, actually I have ADHD so I have a LOT of ideas, all the time (it=E2=80=
=99s practically impossible for me to clean up my home workshop because I w=
ill find some distracting project within 15 minutes of starting, every time=
). AI has been really great for me, at least in one way: it let=E2=80=99s m=
e bring my ideas into reality very quickly. </p><p><span> My team at Micros=
oft has been building a very powerful agentic harness called </span><a href=
=3D"https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier">Amplifier </a><span>for the pas=
t year or so. It has a vast number of </span><a href=3D"https://ramparte.gi=
thub.io/amplifier-stories/">tools </a><span>- architecture experts, reflect=
ive =E2=80=9Csession analyzers=E2=80=9D, a =E2=80=9Cdev foundry=E2=80=9D th=
at I built that stamps out bespoke =E2=80=9Cdev machines=E2=80=9D that can =
work on tasks for days or weeks on their own, and my favorite, the =E2=80=
=9CCrusty Old Engineer=E2=80=9D who is painful but always gives super valua=
ble feedback. </span></p><p>This framework makes it very easy to just start=
 something (and Microsoft gives us a generous token budget - this is expens=
ive!) So my ADHD brain is in heaven - I have many ideas every day and it=E2=
=80=99s very easy to start a project to go investigate them. The harness kn=
ows me, knows its tools, has access to my whole enviroment, and is quite ef=
fective. A few months ago I had a GitHub user with no repos at all. Now I h=
ave over a hundred. The machine is spinning! </p><p>But=E2=80=A6not much of=
 that is fully shipped software. Not because it=E2=80=99s impossible, or ev=
en hard, or that the quality isn=E2=80=99t high. The reality is a bit more =
subtle: shipping, going all the way to robustly done, still involves some t=
hings that aren=E2=80=99t very well =E2=80=9Cagent shaped=E2=80=9D - little=
 bits of fit and finish, context understanding, making sure the final produ=
ct is really what I think it is, etc. Some of this can be mitigated - and I=
 think all of it eventually will be - but right now, the =E2=80=9Clast mile=
=E2=80=9D of releasing something is still too manual. </p><p>The machine of=
 my creativity combined with AI spins. The concrete of shipping sits there,=
 unmoved. </p><p>There are two major areas that my team and I are starting =
to focus on, in our work with these tools. This is the first: that finishin=
g something should be as easy as starting it. I think that=E2=80=99s possib=
le, and I think largely we have all been so enamored of how easy it is to s=
tart things, that we just haven=E2=80=99t focused on it yet. The second are=
a is working together - both many agents working on a problem at once, with=
out causing a mess (so the =E2=80=9Cwall clock=E2=80=9D time to finish it i=
s faster) and people working together in teams. My team of 12 has over 500 =
projects we=E2=80=99ve built - it=E2=80=99s hard even to understand with th=
e help of AI. </p><p>Why am I telling you this? Sounds like a failure - lot=
s of heat and motion but no output. I don=E2=80=99t think it is. I think it=
=E2=80=99s a necessary step along the road - before the current wave of mod=
els, we had the idea of a harness, and some of the pieces, but it wasn=E2=
=80=99t very effective, and we spent our time on that problem. Then we had =
effective models so we could dive deeply into making the harness smarter, s=
elf-improving, and more effective. Now that we largely understand that, we =
have uncovered the next problem - the last mile. All technologies are like =
this - one problem or bottleneck at a time. Solving one reveals the next.</=
p><p>I know there is a lot of backlash and suspicion these days about AI. M=
y experience as a technologist leads me to believe this is misplaced. Yes, =
it=E2=80=99s being used in dumb ways right now, mostly to rent-seek and red=
uce costs. This is largely because those use cases aren=E2=80=99t complex e=
ither to understand or implement. But the work I=E2=80=99ve done with Ampli=
fier has convinced me that there are huge gains waiting for all of us, once=
 we get through the building phase. Last month I used my tools to clone Wor=
d - I=E2=80=99ve already seen one other person do this, and it=E2=80=99s no=
t even particularly interesting now. This week I=E2=80=99ve been working on=
 writing novels - they=E2=80=99re not good yet but they=E2=80=99re getting =
better. I=E2=80=99ve built two different large, complex tools for someone e=
lse, just because it was easy to help them - one for internal use and one f=
or a school in Japan, to help interview students and help them shape ideas =
for AI. </p><p>If you=E2=80=99ve read my writing for any amount of time, yo=
u know that my constant theme is that pessimism usually isn=E2=80=99t very =
valuable, that it=E2=80=99s better to ask =E2=80=9Cwhat if?=E2=80=9D than =
=E2=80=9Cwhy not?=E2=80=9D. Every new mode of being, every new tool, every =
new food or new idea we=E2=80=99ve ever had, was =E2=80=9Cwrong=E2=80=9D be=
fore it was =E2=80=9Cright=E2=80=9D. There are problems with AI still, but =
we are gradually solving them, and it=E2=80=99s already clear to me that th=
ere is huge value every time we solve the next one. Things that were unthin=
kable even a few months ago are routine or even boring now. The gears are a=
ll turning. The block will move, eventually. </p><div data-component-name=
